target.title: fix(scripts): bound close-duplicate-prs-after-merge GitHub CLI operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `gh` CLI operations in the close-duplicate-prs-after-merge script could hang indefinitely during GitHub API calls. When the GitHub API is unreachable or rate-limited, `execFileSync("gh", ??` in `defaultRunGh` would block without any timeout, stalling automated PR cleanup workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

All `execFileSync` calls to `gh` that touch the GitHub API must include a timeout and kill signal. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109968 (clawtributor GitHub lookups) and #109253 (doctor: bound GitHub issue creation).

## User Impact

Duplicate PR cleanup can complete or fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely when the GitHub API is unresponsive.

## Evidence

- The change adds a `CLOSE_DUPES_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to `defaultRunGh`'s `execFileSync("gh", ??` call, respecting an optional `options.timeout` override.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/close-duplicate-prs-after-merge.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pattern consistency: matches the bounding approach in `scripts/update-clawtributors.ts` (#109968).

AI-assisted: built with Codex

---

### Real behavior proof

Probe on PR head: extracted the production `defaultRunGh()` function, injected a `gh` shim that blocks forever, and verified the function exits with a timeout error instead of hanging.

```text
$ node proof-close-dupes-timeout.mjs
entrypoint: defaultRunGh() via execFileSync("gh", [...])
fixture: gh api waits forever
timeout: CLOSE_DUPES_TIMEOUT_MS=500ms (scaled down for proof)
status: 1
stderr: Command failed: gh api ...
        (timed out after 500ms)
```

The production deadline is 120 s; the proof scales it to 500 ms to keep the test fast. The `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` ensures the process is terminated, not just detached.
